# SEO-377: Provide a skip link past repeated navigation

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `accessibility` |
| Category | `ACCESSIBILITY` |
| Minimum level | `RECOMMENDED` |
| Severity | `MEDIUM` |
| Impact | `LOW` |
| Change safety | `REVIEW_REQUIRED` |
| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

Each page offers a mechanism, reachable as the first focusable item, that moves focus past the header and navigation directly to the main content region.

## Rationale

Without it a keyboard reader traverses every navigation item on every page before reaching the content, which makes the repeated block a cost paid once per page rather than once per site.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Place the link first in the document, target the main landmark by identifier, and reveal it on focus rather than hiding it in a way that removes it from the focus order. Confirm focus actually lands in the target region and not merely that the address changed.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Focus the first item on each page, activate it, and record where focus lands relative to the main landmark.
- Evidence: `BROWSER`, `ACCESSIBILITY_SCAN`, `RENDERED_HTML`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: A skip link is one of several mechanisms the cited criterion accepts. A correct landmark structure can satisfy it instead, so the presence of the link is not the only passing outcome.
